Terms of Service

Effective date: November 21, 2026

Last updated: November 21, 2026

These terms are an agreement between you and Xueyan Zhang, an individual doing business as OpenMarkdown in Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada ("OpenMarkdown", "we", "us"). OpenMarkdown is run by one person. There is no company behind it.

We have tried to write this in plain language. If something is unclear, email us at support@openmarkdown.dev and we will explain it.

1. What these terms cover

OpenMarkdown has three parts:

  • The app. The OpenMarkdown desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. It works without an account, and your notes stay as plain .md files in folders you choose.
  • Anywhere. An optional free account that syncs one folder you pick to our servers, so it stays the same on your computers and can be used by an AI app you connect (see section 6).
  • Anywhere+. The paid plan of Anywhere, with more space, larger files and longer history.

If you only use the app without an account, sections 1, 2, 9, 11, 12 and 13 apply to you. The rest is about Anywhere and Anywhere+.

Our Privacy Policy explains what data we handle and why. It is part of these terms.

2. Using the app

You may install and use the app for free, for personal use and for work.

The app is closed-source. Please don't copy, resell or redistribute it, remove our notices, or try to get at its source code, except where the law allows you to do so regardless of what we say here.

We may release updates. The app checks for new versions when it starts (see the Privacy Policy). Some updates may be needed to keep syncing with Anywhere.

3. Your account

  • You need an account to use Anywhere. Sign-in is handled by our sign-in provider, WorkOS.
  • You must be at least 16 years old to create an account, and old enough where you live to agree to these terms.
  • One account is for one person. Keep your sign-in secure. You are responsible for what happens under your account, including what an AI app you connect does with the access you gave it.
  • Tell us quickly at support@openmarkdown.dev if you think someone else has access to your account.

4. Your notes stay yours

You own what you write. We claim no rights in your notes or files.

To run Anywhere, you let us store, copy, transfer and process the files in your synced folder, only as needed to provide the service: keeping your devices in step, keeping history, merging edits, and answering the AI apps you connect. This permission ends when the files are deleted from our servers (see section 8).

We do not sell your notes, show them to advertisers, or use them to train AI models.

5. What Anywhere does, and what it doesn't

  • Only one folder. Only the folder you pick is synced. Everything else on your computer stays there.
  • Encrypted storage, not end-to-end. Your files are encrypted while they travel and while they are stored. The keys are managed by our hosting provider, Cloudflare, not derived from a password only you know. That means our servers can read your notes, which they must do to merge edits and to answer the AI apps you connect. Anywhere is not end-to-end encrypted. Who may look at your notes, and when, is set out in the Privacy Policy.
  • Conflicts. If the same lines are changed in two places, the cloud version stays in the note and the other version is saved next to it as a separate conflict file. We design sync so that no text is lost, but software can fail.
  • History. We keep earlier versions of your notes for a limited time (see your plan). Older versions are thinned out to checkpoints, not every keystroke. History also counts toward your storage.
  • Not a backup. Sync copies changes, including deletions and mistakes, to every device. Please keep your own backups of anything important.
  • Availability. We aim to keep Anywhere running, but we don't promise it will always be available or free of errors. When the service is busy or down, your files stay on your computer and sync resumes later.

6. Connecting an AI app

You can connect an AI app, currently Claude or ChatGPT, to your Anywhere account. Nothing is connected until you do it yourself.

  • Once connected, that AI app can list, search and read the notes in your synced folder, and add to or change them when you ask it to.
  • The AI app is run by its own company (Anthropic or OpenAI) under its own terms and privacy policy. What it receives from your notes is handled by that company, not by us.
  • AI apps make mistakes. Check what they change. History lets you bring an earlier version back while it is still kept.
  • You can disconnect an AI app at any time in that app's settings.

7. Plans, payment and refunds

Plans

  • Anywhere (free): currently 1 MB of cloud space, 1 MB per file and 7 days of history.
  • Anywhere+ (paid): currently 10 GB of cloud space, 50 MB per file and 90 days of history.

Current prices are on our pricing page. Prices include sales tax and VAT where they apply. New accounts may get a lower price for their first year, and we sometimes offer promotion codes. A discount applies only to the payment it is shown for.

Two ways to pay

  • A subscription (yearly or monthly, by card and similar methods). It renews automatically at the end of each period until you cancel. These subscriptions are sold through Stripe's Managed Payments service, which acts as the seller (merchant of record) and handles tax. Stripe's own terms for that purchase also apply.
  • A one-year payment (including Alipay and WeChat Pay). It covers one year and does not renew. If you pay again before it ends, the new year is added after the current one. For these payments we are the seller.

Payments are processed by Stripe. We never see or store your full card number.

Cancelling

You can cancel a subscription at any time from Manage subscription in the app's Account card, or from the Stripe billing page linked on our pricing page using only your email. When you cancel, Anywhere+ stays on until the end of the period you already paid for, then stops. We don't charge cancellation fees.

Refunds

  • 7 days, no questions. If you ask within 7 days of any Anywhere+ payment, including an automatic renewal, we refund that payment in full. Email support@openmarkdown.dev.
  • After 7 days, payments are not refunded, except where the law says otherwise or in section 10.
  • A refund ends the time that payment bought. If what you have stored is then over the free limits, your cloud copy becomes read-only, as in section 8. A refund never deletes your notes by itself.
  • Supporter and Founding Supporter payments are one-time gifts to the project, not a purchase of the service. They are not refundable.

Price changes

If we raise the price of a subscription, we will tell you at least 30 days before your next renewal at the new price. You can cancel before then. A price change never applies to time you have already paid for.

8. When Anywhere+ ends, and deleting your data

If your paid time runs out (you cancelled, a payment failed, a one-year payment ended, or a payment was refunded):

  • If what you store fits the free plan, you simply continue on the free plan.
  • If it doesn't fit, your cloud copy becomes read-only. You can still read it and your AI app can still read it, but nothing new is saved to the cloud. We don't delete anything and don't thin out your history while it is read-only. Renew and sync picks up again straight away.
  • The notes on your computer are never touched. You can keep editing them in the app. They just stop syncing.
  • If your cloud copy stays read-only, we will remind you by email and in the app about 60 days after your plan ended. If you don’t renew or reduce what you store by 90 days after your plan ended, we may delete the cloud copy. The notes on your computer are not affected.

You can delete your cloud copy at any time from the app. This removes your synced notes and their history from our servers. Deleting the cloud copy does not cancel a subscription; cancel that separately (section 7). We keep your account and billing records, as explained in the Privacy Policy.

To close your account entirely, email support@openmarkdown.dev.

9. Fair use

Please don't use OpenMarkdown to:

  • break the law or infringe anyone's rights;
  • store or spread malware, or attack, overload, probe or get around the limits of our servers;
  • get into other people's accounts or data;
  • resell Anywhere, or let anyone else use your account;
  • use automated means to put an undue burden on our servers. Reading and writing your own notes through the AI connection we provide (MCP) is normal use, not a breach of this rule;
  • store content whose possession is itself illegal, such as child sexual abuse material.

10. Suspension, termination and changes to the service

  • You can stop using OpenMarkdown at any time.
  • We may suspend or close an account that seriously or repeatedly breaks these terms, or when the law requires it. Unless the law or a security risk prevents it, we will tell you first and give you time to take your notes out. The notes on your computer are always yours and stay where they are.
  • We may change or stop parts of Anywhere. If we decide to shut down Anywhere+, we will tell you at least 60 days ahead. From that day we stop new purchases and automatic renewals, and we keep Anywhere+ running until all time already paid for has run out, so nobody loses time they paid for. Only if we are forced to stop sooner (for example by law, or because a provider we depend on stops) will we refund the unused part of prepaid time instead.
  • Plan limits may change. If we lower the free plan's limits, we will give at least 30 days' notice. Content already over a new limit becomes read-only, not deleted. Limits on time you have already paid for won't be lowered.

11. No warranty

OpenMarkdown is provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, we make no promises beyond the ones written in these terms, including about fitness for a particular purpose or that it will be free of errors. Some places don't allow these limits, so some of them may not apply to you.

12. Limit of liability

To the extent the law allows:

  • we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, such as lost profits or lost data you could have restored from a backup; and
  • our total liability to you is limited to what you paid or owe us for the service in the 12 months before the claim.

Nothing here limits liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as for fraud or gross negligence, or your rights as a consumer where you live.
